## User story

**As an** operator reviewing a saved scan,
**I want** a retained reference to the aerial crop and any available heatmap behind it,
**so that** I can retrieve the evidence used for that assessment instead of relying only on its textual report.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Uploaded crop remains retrievable**
Given a successful scan and available `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` storage,
when the upload workflow completes,
then the aerial crop is stored in that configured bucket under a deterministic object prefix and its persisted scan-record URI lets an authorized operator retrieve bytes matching the uploaded crop.

**AC2 — Existing heatmaps are retained too**
Given a generated heatmap is already available for the scan,
when artifacts are retained,
then it is stored under the deterministic artifact-prefix convention and its object URI is persisted with the same scan; when no heatmap exists, no generation workflow or false heatmap reference is introduced.

**AC3 — Storage failure does not destroy analysis**
Given object storage is unavailable or one artifact upload fails,
when analysis completes with functioning report persistence,
then a safe warning is logged, the heat report remains successful, and no URI claims successful retention of an artifact whose upload failed.

**AC4 — Saved references survive history retrieval**
Given a scan with successfully retained artifacts,
when I retrieve its saved report through existing scan history,
then the same object references remain available with that report and identify the retained artifacts without exposing image bytes, credentials or raw cloud errors in logs.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add the backlog's proposed storage service with a lazy cached ADC client and environment-selected bucket
- [ ] Agree deterministic prefix and serialized scan-record URI names without inventing new product scope
- [ ] Retain uploaded crop bytes and any already-generated heatmap
- [ ] Compose artifact references into persisted scan records and preserve them through history
- [ ] Continue analysis safely on expected upload failures without recording false successful references
- [ ] Wrap synchronous storage work through `asyncio.to_thread` in the controller
- [ ] Add mocked artifact-integrity, references, missing-heatmap and degradation tests

## Current state

No scan-artifact storage service exists. The API reads image bytes but never uploads them, and the database has no artifact-reference workflow. STORY-031 is blocked on STORY-010 and STORY-006.

| Gap                                                                           | Impact                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Image bytes are discarded after request handling                              | A saved scan does not identify retrievable source imagery                                                              |
| No artifact URIs are composed into scan records                               | History cannot expose the evidence behind a report                                                                     |
| No current heatmap-generation workflow                                        | Retention must be conditional on an artifact already existing, not a new generator                                     |
| Prefix and URI field names are not frozen in the guide's strict report schema | Persisted-record metadata and API response schemas need an agreed compatible extension before tests freeze exact names |

Resolved OQ-3 assigns this workflow to EPIC-005, not the synthetic seeder. The backlog lists the proposed storage service as an expected touch point; it is not linked in the header because the file does not exist yet. Follow the [GCP service instructions](../../instructions/gcp-services.instructions.md) and [FastAPI instructions](../../instructions/fastapi-backend.instructions.md), with the resolved FR-31 best-effort storage policy. Retrieval means authorized access via persisted object references; no new download endpoint, public bucket or signed-URL policy is implied.

## Test cases

| Test                                                                   | Asserts                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_scan_crop_is_retained_with_retrievable_persisted_uri`            | Configured object bytes match the uploaded crop and its URI is saved        |
| `test_existing_heatmap_is_retained_without_generating_missing_heatmap` | Available heatmaps are saved and absent ones remain absent                  |
| `test_artifact_upload_failure_preserves_report_without_false_uri`      | Expected failure is safely logged and successful analysis remains available |
| `test_scan_history_preserves_retained_artifact_references`             | Existing history exposes stable scan/artifact associations                  |

Mock GCS for byte and URI assertions; authorized live retrieval is a separate manual integration check, not an automated cloud call.

## Definition of done

Object-prefix and URI representation are agreed, all four cases pass offline, a separate integration check retrieves the original uploaded bytes using the saved reference, and coverage stays at least 70%. No heatmap generator or extra retrieval API is added. Estimate 3 is retained for conditional retention and record association only.
